# StreamDek Mobile v2.1.11

*Version code 69*

## What's New

- **Animation Speed**
A new setting under **Settings → Appearance and Language → Motion** decides how long transitions
take across the whole app. **Off** changes state immediately, keeping only a brief crossfade so
nothing snaps; **Fast** is shorter and subtler; **Standard** is the recommended balance and the
default; **Cinematic** is slower and fully visible. Changes apply the moment you choose them, with
no restart, and the setting is saved on this device only — it is not synchronized through your
StreamDek account, so your phone and your television can each have their own answer. If your
device's Reduce Motion setting is on it takes priority, and the row says so rather than quietly
ignoring your choice.

- **Branded streaming network cards.** The Streaming Networks row can show each service's own
  artwork edge to edge instead of a logo on a white tile, with artwork for Netflix, Prime Video,
  Disney+, Paramount+, Peacock, Starz, YouTube and more. It follows the same account setting as 
  the TV, so the two match.

## Improvements

**The profile screen opens as one scene**
"Who's watching?" used to appear on its own with a spinner underneath it, the profiles cut into
place when they arrived, and the artwork, title and synopsis faded in separately afterwards. The
whole page is now revealed by a single choreographed sequence: the artwork settles in and its
gradient arrives with it, the category, title and synopsis follow in a gentle stagger, then the
heading, then the profiles from left to right with Add Profile as part of the same run, and finally
Manage Profiles. Profile data and hero artwork load at the same time, and the wait before the
reveal is a restrained ambient glow rather than a spinner under a heading.

Nothing about choosing a profile got slower. Touching the screen at any point lands the rest of the
sequence immediately, so a tap during the reveal is answered at once.

**The Home spotlight blends into the page**
The spotlight used to end at a straight horizontal line: its last row of pixels was flat page
colour while the strip immediately beneath it showed the ambient backdrop, so Home read as two
stacked panels. The artwork now thins out into whatever is behind it instead of being covered over,
and a wash taken from the current title's own colours carries across the join and under the top of
the first row. There is no longer a place to point at where the spotlight stops.

Changing spotlight titles is one transition rather than three: the artwork, the colour and the
gradient now crossfade together, and the previous title's colouring is held until the next one has
actually been read from its artwork — so the background no longer flashes through a default grey
between two titles.

**The splash screen follows your Appearance setting**
A profile pinned to Dark on a light phone opened onto a white splash and then a black app. The app
now tells the system which mode it is in before the starting window is built, so the splash matches
the app on Android 12 and above. Below that the starting window still follows the phone, but the
first screen no longer does.

**One motion system behind every animation**
Screen transitions, expanding sections, the navigation bar, ratings, the trailer handover and the
lists that reorder themselves all now take their timing from one shared set of durations rather
than from numbers written where each animation happened to be. That is what lets a single setting
govern all of them, and it keeps the phone and the television working from the same definition of
what "standard" means. Loading indicators, playback and buffering timing, network timeouts,
long-press thresholds and auto-hide delays are deliberately untouched by it.

**Reduce Motion applies far more widely**
Your device's reduce-motion request previously reached only a handful of animations. It now applies
across the app, replacing movement and scaling with short crossfades rather than removing feedback
altogether.

**Improved subtitles Loading and subtitle delay management on the Media3 player.** Both were previously 
available only on the other playback engine. A subtitle you have loaded from a file, or from an add-on, 
now displays on Media3 too, and its timing can be nudged when it runs ahead of or behind the dialogue.

## Fixed

* Fixed the profile screen showing a heading and a spinner before its content, and the profiles
  then appearing in a single jump.
* Fixed the profile screen's artwork running its own fade whenever the catalogue happened to
  arrive, out of step with everything else on the page.
* Fixed the visible horizontal division between the Home spotlight and the first content row.
* Fixed the blurred Home background replacing itself in a single frame when the spotlight changed.
* Fixed hero text in the light theme having no backing behind it.
* Fixed a light splash screen handing over to a dark app, and the reverse.
